channel.title: Israel National News Flashes
channel.description: Latest news flashes from Israel National News

item.title: Golden remembrance stones
item.description: Two childhoods shatttered in Berlin, two family stories remembered together.

item.title: Netanyahu associate was in contact with Mansour Abbas while PM attacked Ra'am
item.description: As Netanyahu warns against a government dependent on Arab parties, his close associate Natan Eshel has been working behind the scenes to communicate with Mansour Abbas.

item.title: Mysterious Russian plane that landed in Israel was carrying Russian officials
item.description: A source familiar with the details told Kan News that senior Russian officials were aboard the Russian aircraft that landed at Ben Gurion Airport yesterday. According to the report, the landing may have been a stopover en route to a Russia-Ukraine peace summit scheduled to be hosted by the United States in Abu Dhabi tomorrow.

item.title: 'Never Again' faces historic test, German Chancellor warns
item.description: 'Never Again' faces historic test, German Chancellor warns

item.title: 3,039 dunams: Major development project advances in Gush Etzion
item.description: IDF Central Command chief Maj. Gen. Avi Bluth has signed an order establishing the jurisdictional boundaries of a new industrial zone near the Tarkumiya Crossing, which is expected to strengthen Gush Etzion's economy.

item.title: "Historic achievement": Another community officially recognized in northern Samaria
item.description: The Interior Ministry has granted an official locality code to the community of Noa in northern Samaria, completing its regularization process and granting it formal recognition.

item.title: Trump's Board of Peace criticizes Israel, Hamas following Gaza floods
item.description: The Board of Peace calls on Israel to accelerate entry of winter supplies after severe flooding in Gaza, while also demanding that Hamas disarm.

item.title: PA arrests suspects in sale of Jericho homes to Jews
item.description:
A spokesman for the Palestinian Authority security forces confirmed that suspects were arrested for selling houses to Jews near Jericho.
According to the Saudi newspaper "Asharq Al-Awsat", the detainees are intermediaries who were involved in transferring the houses to Jews.

item.title: Board of Peace criticizes both Israel and Hamas
item.description: Following the flooding in Gaza, the Board of Peace called on Israel to accelerate the entry of humanitarian supplies into the Strip, and on Hamas to disarm and transfer power. The council warned that those who fail to meet their commitments will face consequences.

item.title: Voters in 8 Illinois communities back repeal of anti-BDS law
item.description: Voters in eight Illinois communities back nonbinding measures opposing the state's anti-BDS law, despite objections from local Jewish organizations.

item.title: IDF: Over 91,000 tents, 8,200 trucks of winter supplies enter Gaza
item.description: IDF and COGAT advance winter preparations in Gaza, facilitating the entry of shelter equipment, medical supplies, and sanitation infrastructure while working to prevent Hamas from exploiting humanitarian aid.

item.title: France accuses Iran of cyberattack on supermarket refrigerators
item.description: France has accused Iran of responsibility for the cyberattack on supermarket refrigerators and warned that Iran "will bear the consequences."

item.title: Defense Ministry: Flydubai passengers to be recognized as victims of terrorism
item.description: Following official confirmation from investigative authorities, the Defense Ministry has recognized the attempted terrorist attack on a flight to Israel as an act of terrorism and referred the decision to the National Insurance Institute.

item.title: Blinken and Pompeo agree: End of US military aid won't hurt Israel ties
item.description: Former US Secretaries of State Blinken and Pompeo say ending military aid would not weaken US-Israel ties, but disagree sharply over Iran and Gaza.

item.title: Eisonkot or other Yashar MK will be next Knesset Speaker
item.description: The position of the next Knesset Speaker will be given to the Yashar Party and will be filled by party chairman Gadi Eisenkot or a representative on his behalf.

item.title: Liberman, Eisenkot agree on who should be next Knesset Speaker
item.description: In a meeting between Yisrael Beytenu Chairman Avigdor Lieberman and Chairman of the Knesset, Gadi Eisenkot, an agreement was reached on the identity of the next Knesset Speaker. The two have not yet revealed who this is.

item.title: 'We were ready for any mission': Inside the Jewish return to Jericho
item.description: New Jewish residents of Jericho recount how they prepared for a secret mission, discovered their destination, and moved into their newly purchased homes.

item.title: After Democratic victory, Trump questions integrity of midterm elections
item.description: US President Donald Trump casts doubt on the integrity of the midterm elections, claiming that voting machines had a greater influence on the results than the voters themselves.

item.title: Turkish intelligence chief issues warning over Israel's next government
item.description: Turkish intelligence chief Ibrahim Kalin says Israel's next government will reveal whether tensions with Ankara stem from Netanyahu or Israeli policy.

item.title: Jewish belonging should not require a police escort
item.description: Philadelphia’s answer to an antisemitic boycott offers a standard for American leadership after the elections. Op-ed.

item.title: Israelis fear foreign influence. They doubt their government can counter it.
item.description: A government can possess advanced technology, experienced diplomats and substantial intelligence capabilities without persuading foreign audiences that its account of events is credible. Many Israelis feel it is not happening. Op-ed.

item.title: Netanyahu calls for unity government: "Enough with the boycotts, I won't rule snyone out"
item.description: The Prime Minister calls for the establishment of a Likud-led unity government that would include the haredi parties and all Zionist parties.

item.title: Defense Ministry: Flydubai passengers to be recognized as victims of hostilities
item.description: The Ministry of Defense has officially recognized the attempted attack on a FlyDubai flight as a hostile incident. Following the decision, the National Insurance Institute will contact the passengers, who will be recognized as victims of hostile acts.

item.title: Report: NVIDA shares drop by 8%
item.description: Nvidia shares fell about 8% at the opening of trading on Wall Street, after the company's CEO admitted to having an affair with a Chinese spy.

item.title: Mystery in Israel: Russian military plane makes unexplained landing
item.description: A Russian military aircraft makes an unusual landing at Ben Gurion Airport, with Israeli and Russian officials refusing to explain its mysterious visit.

item.title: United Torah Judaism rejects bid to replace Knesset Speaker
item.description: United Torah Judaism tells Gadi Eisenkot’s Yashar! party it won't support early replacement of Knesset Speaker Amir Ohana.

item.title: Police investigate: Who distributed threatening flyers in Tel Aviv?
item.description: Residents of northern Tel Aviv discovered flyers in their mailboxes containing a QR code linking to a website operated by the Handala hacker group.

item.title: Security forces arrest ten terrorists planning attack against Israeli civilians
item.description:
Israeli security forces arrest 10 terror suspects in northern Samaria over allegations of establishing a terror network and planning an attack.
Read more.

item.title: Iran’s leader orders end to ‘neither war nor peace’
item.description: Iran’s President Masoud Pezeshkian says officials told to work toward ending the stalemate, calls for change in approach to improve conditions at home.

item.title: UTJ's red line: No changes on religion and state
item.description: Senior United Torah Judaism official says coalition deal would have to preserve status quo on Shabbat, kashrut, and conversion, in addition to resolving yeshiva students' status.
